description:
Matrix-style digital rain as a real 3D scene, drawn with WebGL 2.0: a camera above water, drops of characters falling at their real distances, their trails fading where they were drawn, splashes flying in 3D, the water's waves simulated in the world and its surface mirroring the scene by them, fog as a medium of 3D clouds, and lightning as a light in it. A clock and a message can be shown, formed by the rain that freezes inside their letters. It also shows what Wallpaper Engine's browser supports: WebGL 2.0, and WebGPU, which works out the drops' layout and draws the readout's panel. In development. Settings marked (Not Implemented) are placeholders for the features of Matrix 3D Rain still to come.

[h1]Support[/h1]
If you can, please sponsor me at https://github.com/sponsors/namakeingo 

[h1]Customizable elements:[/h1]
[list]
    [*]Debug mode: the support readout (what was found of WebGL 2.0 and WebGPU, and where the renderer runs, on a panel drawn by WebGPU); a performance readout (frames a second, the script's and the GPU's time a frame, dropped and missed frames and stalls); a music readout (what Wallpaper Engine's audio carries: its loudness, bass, mid, treble and peak) and simulated music to feed it; an OLED readout (how far the scene, the clock and the message have moved, and the most they may); a view of each pixel's real distance from the camera; the lightning's flash and the splashes switched off; Freeze (nothing drawn or moved, for measuring); a steady start; a strike now at a distance; an HDR line in the support readout (whether the display and the browser could show more than SDR, to see before any HDR output is built)
    [*]OLED pixel shift: every 10 seconds the whole scene moves a pixel left or right, and the clock and the message a pixel in any direction, never further from where they started than the setting, against burn-in
    [*]Frame cap: how many times a second the scene is drawn (24 for the film look)
    [*]Rain: its colors (four custom colors in a gradient across the world, or a rainbow) and the color wave moving them across the world (its speed and width), its characters, its speed, how long its trails last, how bright the drops' heads shine (their extra light, the same at any distance), its size range (Font size Min and Max set the furthest and nearest distances of the drops: 40 m over each) and its density (as many drops in view as Matrix 3D Rain WebGL, spread evenly over each square metre of the world; from a clean screen the rain comes in at its settled rate)
    [*]Bloom: a camera's bloom of the light the drops, splashes and bolt give, spread at four sizes, with no light added or taken away
    [*]Exposure: how bright the camera's picture is, all the light together (the bloom's too) before the tone map, a stop for every 25 steps of the slider
    [*]HDR: shows the picture in real HDR on a display with HDR enabled (needs Post-processing Ultra (Display HDR) in Wallpaper Engine's settings), highlights such as the lightning rising above SDR white; the same picture as before where HDR is not available
    [*]Water: the collision plane (splashes and ripples) and the reflection plane (the mirror image of the rain, the fog and the lightning; the water keeps reflecting the sky and the moon) each on or off, ripples on or off, how much a drop weighs on the water and how long its waves last
    [*]Sky and moon: how bright their light is, one slider for both, and the color of each (the sky seen, and the fog and the water they light)
    [*]Fog: how dense it is, and its two colors
    [*]Lightning: on or off, the average time between strikes, how long each strike plays (its whole animation: the leaders meet a quarter of the way in, then its light fades and flickers), how brightly its bolt shines (it blooms) and, on its own, how brightly its flash lights the fog and the water, the flash's hue from violet to white, and its bolt in 3D, branching on the way down from the clouds and up from the water, as a glowing line with soft edges or as rain characters running along a half-transparent line; Lightning front bias: how much more often strikes land closer to the front (the bolt's foot and top alike), none at 0
    [*]Clock: 24h or 12h, formed by the characters of the rain that freeze inside its digits, laid over the scene; its size and position absolute, or relative to the screen
    [*]Message: custom text, formed by the frozen rain like the clock, shown with the clock or on its own; its size and position absolute, or relative to the screen
    [*]High contrast text: with the color wave, the clock's and the message's characters keep the colors they froze in, or take the color the rain has around them
[/list]

HDR
